record.paper_title: Frequently hypercyclic operators: recent advances and open problems
record.original_question: Do there exist Banach spaces that support a chaotic operator but no frequently hypercyclic operator, or Banach spaces that support a frequently hypercyclic operator but no chaotic operator?

evidence.quote:
Problem 8 (Menet). Are there Banach spaces that support a chaotic operator but n o
frequently hypercyclic operator, or vice versa?

artifact.status_search_result: The question is a space-level separation problem in linear dynamics attributed to Menet. While operator-level separations are known (e.g., Menet constructed a chaotic operator on ℓ^p that is not U-frequently hypercyclic, and Bayart–Grivaux showed frequently hypercyclic operators need not be chaotic), no result has been located that exhibits a Banach space supporting one class but not the other. Surveys on linear dynamics list this as an open problem, and no resolution was found in recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Linear Dynamical Systems (Gilmore survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses chaotic vs. frequently hypercyclic operators, including Menet's construction of a chaotic operator on ℓ^p that is not U-frequently hypercyclic, and outstanding questions about their relationship.
status_evidence.claim: Operator-level separations are known, but the space-level separation question remains discussed as open.

status_evidence.title: Inverse of frequently hypercyclic operators (Menet)
status_evidence.snippet: Menet's work on frequently hypercyclic operators and their relation to chaos.
status_evidence.claim: Menet posed and studied separating questions for chaotic vs. frequently hypercyclic operators.
